text: adversarial finding: Every residue can hold while a player who dies never comes back: the play probe runs in god mode, so the checkpoints and the mod's respawn are never exercised in 06's layered geometry (a cap, the deck, the tower).
adversarial finding: boat-run only proves the boat goes east; 'vehicles fit and can leave' also needs it to back out of the lane's end and return west.
adversarial finding: The command room is only reached through the tower's own ladder shaft, but the objective test teleports into it; the tower climb itself is never played.
adversarial finding: look-dusk-palette measures colour only: an image of mostly sky-coloured emptiness could pass it. The structure (bands top to bottom, where the detail is) must match too.
adversarial finding: The emergent property 'each foundation reads as a distinct fight with cover, height and a flank' has no residue: the caps as first built are flat slabs.

adversarial finding: coop-two can pass while guests can't use the ladders (the ladder code moves characters on the host from their controllers' inputs; a guest's input path differs from the host's keyboard).
adversarial finding: Editor saveability: the level is built only from the editor's own templates plus registered mod entities, which the linter parses; no separate residue needed.
adversarial finding: The hanging-container jump chain is an optional route; the linter proves the jumps are within the rules. Not material.
adversarial finding: 'CS enemies hold every layer' has no residue: all enemies could sit on one layer and every other residue still hold.
adversarial finding: 'CS patrol boats drive the lane by autopilot' is unverified in 06: the boat test only records where the patrols ended.
adversarial finding: Co-op strength for 3 and 4 players rests on the names: nothing checks that 06 has enough [2+] and [3+] enemies to scale.

adversarial finding: Round 3: with respawn, the boat backing out, the tower climb, structure as well as palette, cap cover, guest ladders, layers held, patrols and co-op names covered, nothing material is left that no residue would catch. The remaining risk is in the probes themselves (a harness test that passes for the wrong reason), which FINAL_VERIFY re-examines against the evidence.

The water ladder never engaged: the swimmer's feet were at +91 to +102, past the ladder's foot (+40) plus the 50 px margin.
The shaft climb stalled at feet -689, 69 px above the deck floor, after pausing at the floor: the climber catches on the 60 px hatch. It also rose at about 110 px/s against 190 asked for.
The objective's progress reached 9% in 6.5 s because it counts capped frame dt (0.05 s a frame at about 290 ms a frame).
The boat test couldn't board: the player stood at 4640 and the boat's centre was 260 px away, more than its 220 px reach.
The frame cost ratio is 2.13, and the busiest spot is 283 ms against 133 ms for the baseline.
The palette distance to the concept is 58.2 with luma +36: the overview is much brighter and paler than the dusk concept.
In co-op, the guest never engaged the water ladder (the same foot-depth fault) and ended on the boat's deck at -51.

The frame ratio rose from about 2.5 to 6.26 when enemies went from 33 to 69 and the level from 5800 to 15800 px. Frame cost grows with the whole level, not only with what's on screen, which points at simulation (AI, physics) more than drawing.
The ladder now engages (onLadder 1 in the tower trail) but loses hold between the huge physics steps of 300–2000 ms frames.
The objectives count wall-clock time but cap each step at 1 s, and frames up to about 2 s lose time: 32–59% after 6.5 s.
The tanks were at -21 and -3 hp after the test: unmanned, they died in the deck fighting before the raiders arrived.
The raiders' boat ended at (-51213, 587372), flung out of the level: at 3 fps the explosions and contacts integrate over huge steps.
Most of the frame time is the enemies' AI and physics. Removing the enemies will cut 'other' (non-render) time far more than hiding the set pieces or turning off the lamps.

unknown: whether the engine sets character meshes visible again each frame (the cull runs just before render, so it wins either way)
The enemies account for about 1160 of 1706 draw calls at the measured spot, and most of them are off screen: the engine doesn't cull characters by the camera.
The guest's ladder climb works: feet -333 on the cap.
The objective progress stalls at 35–45% while the player is shot at next to each console (the power guard's minigun stands 70 px from the power console).
The raiders' boat was lost before the boat test began: at x 6976, y +16, sunk after minutes of fire while unmanned.

Hiding off-camera characters' meshes just before each render, and skipping the AI of soldiers more than 2600 px from every player, will bring the frame ratio under about 2, most of the way to the 1.5 limit.

cullFar threw on every render ('object is not extensible'), so no character was ever hidden: draw calls stayed at 1012–1590.
All three objectives reached 100, and the extraction completed after the last one.
The shaft climb engaged (ladder 1) but stopped at feet -446 below the soffit hatch, and the tower climb stopped at the L2 slab: a snag at hatch edges.
The raiders' boat reported at (50931, 358242): a wreck flung out of the world. It was destroyed at the start, where cap 1's and the ledge's guards can see the dock.
Keeping per-character state in WeakMaps and hooking pb2Controller.prototype._bm once makes the culling and the sleep work, cutting most of the characters' draw calls.
Making the climber a ghost while it climbs (its fixtures filtered to collide with nothing, restored when it lets go), with 140 px hatches, removes the snag.
